dispatch.headline: Plague Reenactors Refuse Modern Cure
dispatch.body:
Three historical reenactors are refusing synthetic antibiotics after grafting active bubonic plague nodes onto their thighs.

The three men, who are currently barricaded inside a wicker ox-cart at the annual High-Silt Fair, claim the painful swellings are necessary for tactile period accuracy.

They represent the year 1348.

"We want the authentic limp," said one reenactor, speaking through a gap in the woven wicker.

They have fever.

The regional health guild dispatched a single clerk to resolve the standoff.

She carried a copper vaporiser, a canvas folding stool, and a tube of skin-glue she refused to open during the twelve-hour negotiation.

She has offered them broad-spectrum patch-vaccines.

The men declined.

Under local sanitisation codes, the fair committee must scrub the surrounding soil with vinegar while the cart remains occupied.

The committee has already cancelled the pig-bowling championship to pay for thirty barrels of the cleaning liquid.

Meanwhile, the men have requested three wooden bowls of pease pudding, a cold turnip, and an unwashed priest.

They plan to stay in the cart until Sunday.

glossary.gloss: A self-adhesive dermal square that delivers immunisation through the skin without needles.

drafts.headline: Hikers Blockade Volcanic Trail
drafts.body:
Sixteen bare-chested hikers are blockading the high-altitude sulfur trail on Mount Evans. They are protesting tourists who use synthetic lung-capsules to breathe the volcanic air.

The protest group has pitched three woollen shelters across the main ridge. They brought no filtration gear.

"If you do not cough up black silt, you have not seen the mountain," said climber Kaelen Soto. Soto has spent four hours inhaling the heavy sulfur fumes without a mask. "The capsules are cheating."

On Wednesday, the blockaders turned away forty-two sightseers. The tourists had travelled three hundred kilometres from the floating sea-suburbs to view the active vents. Most tourists wear the internal lung-capsules, which chemically dissolve volcanic ash before it hits the throat.

The protest has halted park operations. Rangers cannot clear the trail because the protesters keep losing consciousness. Two medical gliders have landed to treat the group, but hikers are batting the oxygen hoses away with carbon walking poles.

Soto fell over twice during his interview. He insisted he was fine.

"This is pure nature," he croaked through a thick layer of grey ash. He then threw up.
drafts.premise: DENVER-COAST — Purist wilderness hikers are blockading the high-altitude sulfur trail to protest casual tourists who use synthetic lung-capsules, claiming that inhaling raw volcanic ash is the only honest way to experience nature.
